title: Does Prayer Really Work? Science Says Otherwise
description:
PWhat is prayer, and does it really work? In this episode of Pale Blue Thoughts, we take a critical look at prayer across religions—from Hindu mantras to Christian intercessions and Islamic duas—and ask whether it is anything more than a psychological comfort.

We explore why people pray, how prayers appear to “work,” and why outcomes often match what could naturally happen anyway. From Lourdes in France to Velankanni in Tamil Nadu, millions flock to holy sites hoping for miracles, yet the so-called cures are negligible compared to the vast numbers who remain sick. We also look at how prayer can teach unhealthy habits, normalizing begging and bribing, instead of encouraging real solutions.

Science puts prayer to the test too. The Templeton Foundation’s STEP trial (2006) studied more than 1,800 patients undergoing heart surgery and found no difference in recovery between those prayed for and those who weren’t. In fact, complications were higher in patients who knew prayers were being said for them—anxiety worked against them.

👉 If you’ve searched for does prayer work, scientific studies on prayer, Templeton prayer study, Lourdes miracle cures, power of prayer, prayer vs science, atheist view on prayer — this video gives you the evidence-based perspective.

This is because, to fulfil the devotees' prayers god will have to alter his decrees and change the future predestined by god himself. That means god doesn't know the future with certainty as god himself is forced to alter the future at the demand of the prayers from mere mortals. That is, god is helpless at the demands of devotees and has no other choice but to alter the future he determined beforehand. Thus god doesn't know the future!!! And if he doesn't know the future, he is not all-knowing. 

Also, if he changes his decrees and alters the future he destined in advance, he is not even all-powerful!!! One who cannot save his decrees from getting nullified and altered by external demands in the form of prayers from devotees is not all-powerful. 

To sum it up, the act of praying is not compatible at all with the qualities of "all-knowing" and "all-powerful" that people attribute to god.
